The immediate precursor to the rupee is the rūpiya—the silver coin weighing 178 grains minted in northern India, first by Sher Shah Suri during his brief rule between 1540 and 1545, and later by the Mughal Empire. Banksman.question: What is Banksman? Civil engineering profession.
Banksman.fact: In Irish and British civil engineering, a banksman is the person who directs the operation of a crane or larger vehicle from the point near where loads are attached and detached.

Boilermaker.subject: Business & Economy
Boilermaker.question: What is Boilermaker? Tradesperson who fabricates steel, iron, or copper into boilers.
Boilermaker.fact: A boilermaker is a tradesperson who fabricates steels, iron, or copper into boilers and other large containers intended to hold hot gas or liquid, as well as maintains and repairs boilers and boiler systems.   Although the name originated from craftsmen who made boilers, boilermakers assemble, maintain, and repair other large vessels and closed vats, in addition to boilers.

Bricklayer.subject: Business & Economy
Bricklayer.question: What is Bricklayer? Person who lays brick.
Bricklayer.fact: A bricklayer, which is related to but different from a mason, is a craftsperson and tradesperson who lays bricks to construct brickwork.   In British and Australian English, a bricklayer is colloquially called a "brickie".

Builders' rites.fact: Builders' rites are ceremonies attendant on the laying of foundation stones, including ecclesiastical, masonic or other traditions connected with foundations or other aspects of construction.

Building code.subject: Business & Economy
Building code.question: What is Building code? Construction standards for buildings.
Building code.fact: A building code (also building control or building regulations) is a set of rules that specify the standards for construction objects such as buildings and non-building structures.   The main purpose of building codes is to protect public health, safety and general welfare as they relate to the construction and occupancy of buildings and structures — for example, the building codes in many countries require engineers to consider the effects of soil liquefaction in the design of new buildings.

Building engineer.subject: Business & Economy
Building engineer.question: What is Building engineer? Construction profession.
Building engineer.fact: A building engineer is recognised as being expert in the use of technology for the design, construction, assessment and maintenance of the built environment.   Commercial Building Engineers are concerned with the planning, design, construction, operation, renovation, and maintenance of buildings, as well as with their impacts on the surrounding environment.

Building material.fact: Building material is material used for construction.   The manufacturing of building materials is an set up industry in many countries and the use of these materials is typically segmented into specific specialty trades, such as carpentry, insulation, plumbing, and roofing work.
